known_facts_book1: A live Scarecrow of straw with a stuffed sack for a head, once made by a Munchkin farmer and lifted off his pole by Dorothy, who ruled the Land of Oz for a brief period.
Is asked to take Ozma's place as Ruler while she is away, and **consents at once without asking any questions**.
Is found playing croquet with Trot and Betsy when Glinda arrives, stumbles over a wicket and falls flat on his painted face mid-sentence, and continues talking as if nothing had happened.
Says plainly he has never raised a sunken island in all his life, and asks to be told what to do.
Proposes the one sensible move at the council: go to the Skeezer country and examine it carefully.
Answers the boasting Diamond Swan with 'Handsome is as handsome does. Are your deeds lovely, Coo-ee-oh?'
Falls often on the forest march but is easily patted back into shape, and recites poems at Glinda's reception.
Climbs to the top of the Great Dome with the Patchwork Girl at the end and replaces the pane of glass.

known_facts_book1: A girl made of a gaudy patchwork quilt cut to shape and stuffed with cotton, so full of fun and mad pranks that stupider folks think her crazy — but very intelligent, and much wisdom can be found in her careless remarks.
Is one of Ozma's counsellors, jolly under all conditions however grave, and her good spirits are valued for cheering others.
Predicts of Button Bright that some day he won't be found, and that will be the last of him.
Proposes at the council, laughing, that they pump the water out of the lake, and is told to be sensible.
**Her joke is the solution.** She says that if the lake were dried up the island would be on dry land, and Glinda takes it seriously: lower the water until the Dome shows above it.
Follows up by suggesting the fishes be transformed to polliwogs and given a teeny pond, and is severely refused by the Wizard on principle.
Says 'All right, I don't care' and makes a face at him, and is proved right anyway.
Is as light as a feather and very spry on the march, is loved by the Adepts for her antics, and helps the Scarecrow replace the Dome's glass at the end.

known_relations_book1.Glinda: Who finds real value in her idea.
known_relations_book1.Trot: Who drags her into Glinda's tent to tell it.

known_facts_book1: An enormous lion, one of Ozma's regular guardians and the most important and intelligent beast in all Oz.
Says every little danger scares him so badly that his heart thumps against his ribs, but always summons the courage to meet it — and afterward moans and trembles and weeps because he was so scared.
Joins the expedition unasked, saying that if Ozma needs help he is going to help her, and that the others may need him — especially Trot and Betsy — in the wild Gillikin country.

**Leads the party through the Great Gillikin Forest**, the nearest thing to a wilderness in all Oz, following beast-paths only his woodcraft can discern, and keeps the wild denizens off the travelers.
Admits certain parts of that forest are unknown even to him.
Sings a song in his deep bass voice at Glinda's reception for the Adepts.
Never reaches the sunken island: he stays with the camp on shore.

known_facts_book1: A cat of transparent glass, made and brought to life by Dr. Pipt — who is no longer permitted to work magic and is now an ordinary citizen of the Emerald City.
Has a ruby heart one can watch beating, pink brains that whirl in the top of her head, emerald eyes and a fluffy spun-glass tail.
Scorns to catch mice, does not eat, and is extremely lazy; her ruby heart is hard and cold and her disposition is not pleasant at all times.
Loves admiration above everything, and will be very friendly to anyone who compliments her beauty.
Is seized in an enormous leopard's jaws in the Great Gillikin Forest; the leopard breaks several teeth, howls and drops her, and she is annoyed only by his impudence.
Is sent by Glinda — whom she genuinely fears, unlike everyone else whose orders she ignores — to fetch Button Bright, and does it at once.
Is complained of by Button Bright for being impolite, which he says would count as an insult if she had any manners.
Wants to join the expedition of her own accord, overhearing the conversation, and the Wizard makes no objection.

known_facts_book1: A fine, manly little boy called Button Bright because no one can remember any other name for him, well mannered and good humored, with one bad fault: he is continually getting lost.
Gets found as often as he gets lost, which does not stop his friends worrying.
Wanders off the forest march while trailing at the end throwing twigs at squirrels, and is found asleep under a tree with a tiger crouched on one side and a gray wolf on the other.
Is saved by Glinda's incantation, which fixes both beasts to the ground where they lie.
Wakes, is frightened for a moment, sees the beasts cannot reach him, then **deliberately kicks the tiger's head and whacks the wolf with a branch** before wandering carelessly away.
Is forbidden by Glinda ever to get lost again, and replies that it won't be his fault if he does — and that it wasn't his fault this time.
Says of the Diamond Swan that the old Swan is too much in love with herself to think of anything else.
Suggests using the boat to catch the three fishes, and is told it will not be necessary.

known_facts_book1: A Munchkin boy of about Button Bright's age, called Ojo the Lucky because good fortune follows him wherever he goes.
Is a close friend of Button Bright although of a very different nature, and both are liked by Trot and Betsy.
**Notices first that Button Bright is missing**, and gives the account of when he last saw him.
Asks whether the lost boy can be saved when everyone else has given him up.
Spots the stranded submarine on the far shore of the lake and proposes rowing all over the lake calling to the magic fishes.

known_facts_book1: Two little girls who live at Ozma's palace under her protection, great friends of Dorothy and much loved by all the Oz people.
Are the two friends Dorothy longs to tell about the journey and does not, having promised Ozma to keep it secret.
Are playing croquet with the Scarecrow when Glinda's chariot descends, and Trot says at once that Glinda never comes unless something has gone wrong.
Beg the Wizard to let them join the rescue expedition and are allowed to.
Take turns winding up Tik-Tok's machinery on the march, since it keeps running down.
**Trot is the one who brings Scraps's idea to Glinda**, dragging the Patchwork Girl into the tent between them.
Says of the Diamond Swan that the Su-dic ought to have made her a toad instead, since being beautiful does not seem like much of a punishment.
Share a tent at the camp and are sent away by Glinda while the grown magic-workers plan.
